intro: Jobs similar to brownfield redevelopment specialists are environmental planning, science and engineering roles. By O*NET 31.0 data, the closest are Environmental Restoration Planners (82% similar), Foresters (82%) and Environmental Engineers (79%).
shared: These careers share site assessment, environmental rules and coordinating cleanup or land use with many partners. O*NET rates complex problem solving at 4.12 out of 5 for this job, and coordination and judgment at 4. Restoration planning, forestry, conservation and water resource work rely on the same skills. BLS reports this job only within a broader group earning $141,900, so pay is not compared directly.

faq.q: Which jobs like brownfield redevelopment pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 20 similar careers, Water Resource Specialists have the highest figure at $167,220, followed by Environmental Engineers at $107,110, according to BLS May 2025 data. Brownfield specialists are reported within a broader BLS group, so these are not direct comparisons.

faq.q: Do jobs like brownfield redevelopment need a degree?
faq.a: Most do. Only 1 of the 20 similar careers usually needs less preparation: government property inspectors and investigators. Environmental Restoration Planners, the closest match at 82% similar, usually need a graduate degree, and most of the others usually need at least a bachelor's degree in science or planning.
